description.narrative: People affected by the ILOT conflict and its ramifications

The appeal supports four National Societies, the Egyptian Red Crescent, the Lebanese Red Cross, the Syrian Arab Red Crescent and the Jordan National Red Crescent, in complementarity with the PRCS operation in Gaza,

The appeal was launched on 18 October 2023 to support the coordination and scale-up of the response to the crisis in the countries surrounding the occupied Palestinian territories. It complements the Palestine Red Crescent Society operation by supporting the Egyptian Red Crescent Society, the Lebanese Red Cross, the Syrian Arab Red Crescent and the Jordan National Red Crescent Society, with a target of 1,363,821 people across the four countries. Its two structuring lines are the humanitarian supply corridors into Gaza through Egypt and Jordan, and the response to displacement and spillover in Lebanon and Syria. Please find attached the Operational Strategy, which sets out the plan in detail.

The first axis is logistics: building and running the Egyptian and Jordanian corridors into Gaza through hubs, warehousing, bonded storage, handling equipment and fleet, so that humanitarian supplies can be received, consolidated and dispatched to PRCS when access allows. Its second axis is direct assistance to people affected by the spillover, which since September 2024 has shifted from preparedness to scaled-up response in Lebanon and Syria, covering emergency shelter and core relief items, food assistance, multi-purpose cash, emergency medical services and primary and secondary healthcare, MHPSS, blood transfusion services and WASH, alongside support to Palestinians medically evacuated from Gaza and their families. Protection, gender and inclusion, community engagement and accountability, and restoring family links run across all of it, with particular attention to unaccompanied children, female-headed households, older persons and people with disabilities and chronic illnesses. The largest single budget line, CHF 48.18 million, is National Society strengthening, meaning volunteer duty of care, branch development, logistics infrastructure and emergency operations capacity, which reflects a deliberate choice to keep the four National Societies able to respond as the crisis evolves rather than to move prematurely into recovery.

n Gaza the humanitarian situation remains catastrophic, with mass displacement, near-total collapse of the health system and severe restrictions on the entry of relief. The strategy records that, as of November 2024, the conflict had caused more than 44,380 fatalities, displaced nearly two million people and damaged some 360,000 homes, with 40 percent of the population at high risk of famine and 1.84 million people in acute food insecurity, including 133,000 in catastrophic conditions. Access remains the binding constraint: limited crossing points, restrictions on permitted items, fuel shortages and warehouse congestion slow the pipeline and drive up costs, which is precisely why the logistics capacity of ERCS and JNRCS is central to this appeal.
The regional spillover compounds the picture. In Lebanon the escalation from September 2024 displaced over 1.2 million people, damaged essential water, electricity, road and telecommunications infrastructure, forced health facilities to close and caused damage estimated at over one billion US dollars, while cholera and other outbreaks added pressure on an already overstretched system. In Syria, arrivals from Lebanon exceeded 500,000, straining a fragile socio-economic context and the capacity of SARC to absorb new caseloads. Across all four countries, the people most exposed are displaced households and host communities, unaccompanied and separated children, female-headed households, older persons, people with disabilities and those with chronic illnesses.
